facts.fact: Eswatini's Senate considered its Finance Committee report on the proposed National Payment System Regulations, 2026, which would let the Central Bank of Eswatini designate important payment systems and examine payment service providers.
The proposed National Payment System Regulations, 2026, before Eswatini's Senate, include consumer protection provisions alongside electronic funds transfers and payment service provider obligations.

SWZ.note: Only a general remark on transacting internationally; no corridor or regional system stated.
Nothing on government payments to people.

facts.fact: The Senate considered the Finance Committee report on the National Payment System Regulations, 2026, regulations to operationalise the National Payment Systems Act, 2023, with House of Assembly amendments described by the finance minister as mainly corrections and typographical changes.

SWZ.note: Apple Pay mentioned only as an example of platforms; no mobile money or e-money service in service stated.
Nothing on tax or fee payment.
